Thanks for the ping. Quick notes after initial triage:
- I pulled ingest and runtime traces for CheckoutPlus between 07:30-08:30 PT. I see an uptick in retry cascades originating from a client-side CloseFrame events that our parser is treating as an abrupt stream termination in a subset of cases. The pattern matches their "failed to parse chunk headers" reports.
- We did deploy a parser strictness improvement yesterday to reduce false-positive header merging (change id: PR#8721). That change tightens header boundary detection and rejects borderline framings that previously worked by chance.
- In addition there was a kernel selector tweak rolled to a small canary (10%) overnight that modifies batching window heuristics. This can increase tokenization latency for skewed short/long sequences.

Immediate mitigation options:
1) Revert parser strictness to permissive-mode for CheckoutPlus via routing-config override (quick rollback, low risk).
2) Disable the kernel selector tweak for their dedicated pool (requires infra access, ~30m).
3) Provide a client-side guidance doc for SDK framing flags; we can push a short patch but that will take longer to adopt.

I've attached a short profiler trace and the relevant server logs. Recommend we apply (1) immediately and (2) if p99 stays high.

-Jonas

Attachments referenced: profiler-trace-0518.zip (compressed traces), sdk-logs-0518.txt

Subject: Re: Urgent: CheckoutPlus live traffic — sudden p99 latency and chunked errors from SDK

Eva —

Thanks again for your patience while we investigated. Short update and actions we've taken:

What we found:
- A parser strictness change (PR#8721) introduced tighter header/chunk-boundary detection which caused certain client framings (seen in CheckoutPlus SDK v1.4.2) to be rejected, leading to early stream termination errors for ~2% of requests.
- A kernel selector canary contributed to elevated p99 under CheckoutPlus's sequence-length mix; they hit the canary nodes which increased tail latency.

Immediate steps we've implemented (complete):
- Rolled CheckoutPlus routing to the permissive parser variant (rollback of PR#8721) — this reduced parse errors to under 0.2% in our test window.
- Disabled the kernel selector tweak for their dedicated pool — p99 dropped from ~4.8s -> ~1.6s in the last 30 minutes.
- Kept a passive capture running and attached traces/logs to JIRA INF-4821 for post-mortem.

Next steps:
- We will publish a recommended SDK-framing note for CheckoutPlus and propose a minor SDK patch to make framing explicit (timeline: 3 business days).
- Engineering will run a targeted regression test against their traffic profile before we re-enable the stricter parser.
- I'll coordinate an exec summary for your leadership and ours — Marissa, Ben, please prepare a short one-pager for Friday's leadership sync.

Apologies for the disruption — we're treating this with high priority and will share the post-mortem once complete. If you want a quick call to walk through mitigations and timeline, we're available now.

Best,
Kimberly Park
